description: Ceremony check: for each of the 8 example files, would the file's OWN structure catch a substitution of every concrete citation/evidence with generic advisory-sounding prose?
quoted_language: clear-start.md: "The critic found 5 attacks, conceded one, and two were decision-changing" / unclear-start.md: "a shared buy-gate rule silently bypassed for intraday, and a schema-tolerance fix that reached one pipeline's loaders but not the other's" / heterogeneous-and-homogeneous-roster.md: "`node src/runner/dispatch.mjs decide claude-bwrap --has-live-task-access` returns `{\"mechanism\":\"out-of-process\",\"configured\":false}`" -- versus alternative-and-composite-reopen.md, whose only load-bearing anchor is one link: "See [`synthesis.md`](...) for the real, full treatment of all three plus the critic's attacks against each."
evidence: 6 of 8 files are strongly load-bearing: they carry counted findings, verbatim quotes in the person's own language, named defects, or a runnable command whose output is quoted. Substituting generic prose into any of those six breaks a check anyone can run. The two weakest by this test are (a) alternative-and-composite-reopen.md -- both worked turns are constructed, both classifications are restatements of the SKILL.md table, and the only falsifiable content is the three-proposal roll-up in its opening section (which is itself inaccurate, see RT-P04.2-07); and (b) clarification-and-challenge.md's second half, whose challenge is constructed. Both disclose their constructed status honestly in the first three lines, which is why this is WEAK and not FAILS -- the reader is never misled about what is real. Not a blocker.

description: Designated-loser check: is the constructed `challenge` a softball the panel was always going to handle, or something a real person would actually push back on?
quoted_language: "You're recommending we harden the launcher coordination because it keeps our options open -- but isn't that the same as saying the multi-process split becomes 'the thing that works,' and gets harder to walk back the more we invest in it? What would actually change your mind here?"
evidence: Verified against the real artifact, not the example's own summary. P01.2/critiques/architecture-critic.md:23 states the identical substance: "By successfully engineering this coordination, you deeply entrench the multi-process architecture ... The architecture is only highly reversible if you do *nothing*; fixing the bugs cements the path." P01.2/synthesis.md:77 titles it "Attack 1 -- 'Stay Thin' Reversibility Illusion (architecture-critic; HIGH decision impact) -- **LIVE**", and synthesis.md:69 concedes "Attack 1 was never answered." So the constructed challenge targets the single strongest unrebutted attack in the real session -- the opposite of a softball. Decisively, the example's FIRST taught outcome is that the panel cannot win this one: "this is the same open disagreement the panel already named and did not resolve -- nothing new has been argued on either side since." A designated-loser challenge would have been written so the panel could refute it; this one is written so the panel must admit it is stuck.

description: Promises-more-than-the-graph-delivers check: does ANY sentence imply a reader could obtain a manual-playbook Phase-3-style reopen (fresh scout/shaper dispatch) from the registered protocol?
quoted_language: Heading: "What the manual playbook actually did (real, and no longer available as-is)". Body: "`phase-dialogue-reopen` offers exactly three operations: `revise-synthesis`, `revise-explanation`, `close-dialogue`. There is no operation that re-dispatches the context investigator."
evidence: Read line by line hunting for an over-promise; found none. The divergence is disclosed in the file's own first paragraph ("this file's own second half is a deliberate, disclosed rewrite"), the heading marks the real behavior as unavailable, and the graph limit is stated as an absolute ("There is no operation that..."), matching architecture-advisory-panel-v1.yaml lines 512-530 exactly (phase-dialogue-reopen declares only those three refs, transitions: []). The file then routes the honest case to a NEW coordinationId rather than to any reopen. The how-to guide's own §"This protocol's reopen is narrower than the manual playbook's was, on purpose" says the same thing independently. No sentence in either file promises a Phase-3 reopen.

description: Real-diversity check: does the homogeneous fallback quietly collapse role isolation (shared context/session) rather than only sharing a provider? Checked against the actual request JSON fragment, not the prose describing it.
quoted_language: The homogeneous `actors[]` array declares 8 separate entries, each a distinct `-actor` id: `{ "id": "lead-advisor-actor", "executor": "claude", "tier": "critical" }` ... `{ "id": "red-team-actor", "executor": "claude", "tier": "critical" }`. Prose: "Homogeneous means 'same provider,' never 'same context or session.'"
evidence: The JSON itself is the proof, not the prose: 8 discrete actor entries preserve all 8 static protocol actors, so the engine still creates 8 separate Assignments with 8 separate prompt packages. Nothing in the fragment merges roles, reuses an assignment, or grants cross-role context (`grantedContextRefs` is not used here at all). No `model` key appears anywhere in either roster, consistent with SKILL.md's `assertModelSupportedForKind` rule. The file additionally names what is genuinely lost ("no provider-family diversity to hedge against a shared blind spot") and makes saying so mandatory, quoting the coordinator prompt's real STOP CONDITION. This is real diversity accounting, not cosmetic.

description: Evasive-recommendation check: could a person reading ONLY the how-to guide come away thinking a 'balanced menu' (options presented, no recommendation) is an acceptable panel outcome?
quoted_language: Phase table, row 7: "The synthesizer recommends ONE thing, keeping live disagreement visible rather than smoothing it into a footnote."
evidence: The guard is present and unambiguous in the person-facing doc: "ONE thing" is set in caps in the one row a person actually reads about convergence, and it is immediately paired with the anti-flattening clause so a reader cannot resolve the tension by concluding 'so it just lists options honestly.' The two example families a person is most likely to open next reinforce it from both directions: clear-start.md shows a real single recommendation that still carried a live dissent, and unclear-start.md shows the ONE legitimate exception handled correctly -- "The synthesis correctly refused to pick between three competing mechanisms for one remaining seam when no shaper had produced a fact that would separate them -- it named the missing observation instead of authoring a tiebreak nobody had earned." That is a refusal WITH a named settling observation, which is exactly not a balanced menu.

description: Live check of the cell's founding premise (Step 1, 'no new verb needed'): independently run a real request against `core.coordination-protocol.architecture-advisory-panel-v1` through plain `fgos coordination run --file`, and confirm `fgos coordination show --json` genuinely gives useful orientation across a genuine second CLI invocation.
target_file: docs/how-to/use-fgos-architecture-panel.md (§Resuming a session later; §Do you need a new use-case or CLI verb for any of this?)
quoted_language: "the exact roster still missing quorum (`quorum.missing`), by real actor id -- `lead-advisor-actor` still showed missing even after its own `interpret-request` step reported `\"done\"`" and "No `decision-request.md`/`session.md`/`interpretation.md` was needed to know what to do next"
evidence: Independently reproduced from scratch in a throwaway stub-executor sandbox, session `rt_aap_entry_1`, without reusing the Doer's fixture. Call 1 (`interpret-request` + `investigate-context`) exited 0. `fgos coordination show rt_aap_entry_1 --json` then reported, with zero chat history: quorum.missing = 7 actors INCLUDING `lead-advisor-actor` despite its `interpret-request` step reporting "done" (the multi-operation quorum behavior the guide describes -- confirmed real, not a quirk); pendingDriverAuthorizations naming every gated node/operation; eventCount 13. Call 2, a genuinely separate CLI invocation against the same coordinationId with the three Phase-5 shapers, exited 0, eventCount grew 13 -> 19, and quorum.missing correctly shrank to 5. Separately confirmed the `human-turn` request step works through this same door: it was accepted and the engine computed `revision: sha256:414f08fe...` from the artifact file's real bytes, exactly as clarification-and-challenge.md claims. The entry and resume premise is genuine. NOTE: this attack is what surfaced RT-P04.2-08 -- the proof cited in the guide only ever reached 5 rounds and therefore could not have detected the failure that begins at round 11.

description: Citation accuracy spot check: verify claims that cite a specific P01.2/P01.3 moment against the real proof artifacts.
quoted_language: VERIFIED EXACT: (a) clear-start.md "The critic found 5 attacks, conceded one, and two were decision-changing"; (b) clear-start.md's explanation quote "But do not start with the launcher work. Start by getting the shell into CI..."; (c) final-decision-and-defer.md's two Vietnamese turns and the "permission, not instruction" classification; (d) clarification-and-challenge.md's "giai thich lai cau hoi". DRIFT: alternative-and-composite-reopen.md "Three independently shaped, genuinely different proposals reached the person: **stay-thin-and-fix** ..., **stay-thin-smaller-path** (the same direction, deliberately smaller scope), and **delete-entirely** (drop the shell)."
evidence: Four of five checks verify exactly. (a) P01.2/critiques/architecture-critic.md contains exactly 5 "Decision impact:" entries, two marked High (lines 25, 41), and one explicit concession (line 15: "I must concede this attack fails"). (b) explanation.md:13 and :22 match the quoted fragments verbatim. (c) human/2-person.md:11,18 carry both turns verbatim; dialogue/2-impact.md:70 carries the classification verbatim ("is **permission, not instruction**"). (d) P01.3/human/1-person.md:4 matches. THE DRIFT: `ls P01.2/proposals/` returns exactly three files -- system-shaper.md, alternative-shaper.md, constraint-advocate.md. alternative-shaper.md contains BOTH "## The Candidate: Delete the Experiment" AND "## The Smaller Path: The 'Launcher Fix' (Strict Thin Client)" -- i.e. delete-entirely and stay-thin-smaller-path are two arms of ONE shaper's single proposal, not two independent proposals. constraint-advocate.md's own distinct candidate ("Keep Authority in the Daemon; Repair Desktop Attachment") is not represented in the example's three at all. This matters beyond pedantry: the file's stated purpose is to exercise `request-composition` "against real candidate material rather than invented options," but the composition it then constructs (smaller-scope scope + the other proposal's launcher fixes) combines two arms of the SAME shaper's proposal, which is not what a cross-proposal composition is.

description: Own attack: run the documented request shapes literally, all the way through Phase 9, instead of stopping where the cited proof stopped. Does the Decision Dialogue the how-to and four example files document actually dispatch?
target_file: docs/how-to/use-fgos-architecture-panel.md and all 8 files under docs/how-to/coordination-examples/ (no file declares `aggregateBounds`); core/skills/fgos-architecture-panel/SKILL.md
quoted_language: how-to: "**The two-reopen budget is real, not a suggestion.** `revise-synthesis` and `revise-explanation` are each hard-capped at 2 invocations by the protocol itself (`activation.maxInvocations: 2`) -- a mid-session crash and resume does not reset it, and neither does asking nicely." -- and final-decision-and-defer.md: "`close-dialogue`, the lead advisor's own third gating binding, and the ONLY thing that brings this actor -- and, once every other actor is already settled, the whole session -- to quorum completion".
evidence: Reproduced live end to end. `src/verbs/coordination/schema.mjs:79` sets a DEFAULT `aggregateBounds.maxRounds: 10` for any request that does not declare its own. The protocol's mandatory pre-dialogue path is exactly 10 operations (interpret, investigate, 3 shapers, critique, assess-constraints, synthesize, red-team, explain) = 10 rounds. In session `rt_aap_entry_1`, built with the documented shapes and no `aggregateBounds`, `explain-recommendation` succeeded as round 10 and then EVERY Phase-9 operation was refused at the dispatch door: `fgos: createSessionAssignment: session "rt_aap_entry_1" has already used 10 round(s) session-wide, at or above the declared aggregateBounds.maxRounds cap of 10 -- refusing to create a new Assignment for a new round` (exit 4), identically for `revise-synthesis` (twice) and for `close-dialogue`. Consequence: a coordinator who follows these examples literally gets a session in which the entire documented Decision Dialogue is unreachable, AND -- because `close-dialogue` is the only route to lead-advisor quorum -- the session can never reach quorum completion at all, even for a pure `decide` turn that consumes no reopen. Confirmed a doc defect and not an architecture defect: an otherwise identical session (`rt_aap_bounds_2`) opened with `"aggregateBounds": {"maxRounds": 20, "maxAssignments": 30}` ran all 11 operations including `close-dialogue`, exit 0, and `show` reported `status: completed`, `quorum.missing: []`. The knowledge existed in-repo and did not transfer: test/verbs/coordination-architecture-advisory-panel-conformance.test.mjs passes `{ aggregateBounds: { maxRounds: 20 } }` at both call sites and comments the reason at line 202 ("`aggregateBounds.maxRounds` is raised at open time: this full chain dispatches 12 real Assignments, above the default session-wide cap of 10") and line 833. `grep -rn aggregateBounds docs/how-to/ core/skills/fgos-architecture-panel/` returns zero matches. Also note the second-order effect on the how-to's own resume evidence: the cited live proof (`aap_entry_proof_1`) ran only Phase-1 + Phase-5 (5 rounds), so it was structurally incapable of catching this.

description: Own attack: the flagship example (the first one a reader opens) shows a request with no `actors[]` at all and comments approvingly on its absence. Does that model the exact single-provider collapse phase-04's Requirements forbid?
quoted_language: "Note what is absent: no `actors[]` override naming a bwrap-wrapped executor here -- see the [heterogeneous/homogeneous example](...) for that shape and its own live registration caveat; this file stays focused on the entry/framing mechanics."
evidence: phase-04's Requirements state the skill "never collapses the panel to one session-wide provider or silently defaults every role to the same model when alternatives are configured." A request with no `actors[]` does precisely that: in my live run of this exact shape, both dispatched roles resolved to `"provider": "claude"` on the single global default executor, and the full-chain run reported `provider=/home/vantt/.local/bin/node model=m` for every role. The note quoted above tells the reader only that a bwrap executor name is absent and frames the omission as scope discipline; it never says that what remains runs every advisory role on one provider with no diversity at all. A coordinator who copies the flagship example gets the collapsed roster silently. WEAK rather than FAILS because the omission is genuinely deliberate and cross-linked, the sibling roster example carries the full warning, and SKILL.md's WARNING is unmissable -- but the one-line fix (say what the absence costs, not just what it avoids) is cheap and belongs in the file a reader opens first.

description: Own attack: internal consistency of the person-facing reopen budget. Does the how-to's Decision Dialogue table describe the same budget its own body paragraph describes?
quoted_language: Table column header: "Costs one of your two reopens?" -- versus the paragraph immediately below it: "`revise-synthesis` and `revise-explanation` are each hard-capped at 2 invocations by the protocol itself".
evidence: The column header frames a single shared pool of two reopens; the body correctly describes two independent caps of 2 (up to four reopen dispatches). Confirmed live: `revise-synthesis` accepted two authorizations and refused the third with `authorizeOperation: binding (node "phase-dialogue-reopen", operation "revise-synthesis", actor "synthesizer-actor") ... already has 2 "operation-authorized" event(s), at or above its declared activation.maxInvocations cap of 2`, i.e. the cap is genuinely per-binding, not session-wide. The table under-promises rather than over-promises, so no reader is misled into expecting capability that does not exist -- but it is an inconsistency inside a single section, and 'your two reopens' is the phrase a person will remember. Header should read "Costs a reopen invocation?".
